title.en: Parts of a plant and their jobs (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en:
Ishaan pulled a small weed from the garden. It came out with a thin white root, a green stem, a few leaves and a tiny flower.
"Each part looks different," he said. His grandmother explained, "Each part has its own job."

The root grows in the soil. It holds the plant firmly and takes in water and minerals from the soil.
The stem carries water and minerals up to the leaves and carries food from the leaves to other parts. It also holds the leaves and flowers up to the light.
Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight, air and water. This is called photosynthesis. The flower makes seeds, which can grow into new plants.
The root holds the plant in the soil and takes in water and minerals.
The stem carries water up and food to all parts of the plant.
Leaves make food using sunlight, air and water. This is photosynthesis.
The flower makes seeds that grow into new plants.

problem.en: What will happen to a plant if its roots are cut off?

text.en: Roots take in water and minerals from the soil.
Without roots the plant cannot get water, and it cannot stand firmly.
So the plant will wilt and die.

prompt.en: A friend says leaves only make the plant look beautiful. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: Leaves make food for the plant by photosynthesis.
They use sunlight, air and water.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking leaves are only for decoration.

points.en: Root holds the plant and takes in water.
Leaves make food; the flower makes seeds.
